name: venue
description: What a venue is and how to learn about the one you are on: identity (name, DID, URL), how clients connect, what it offers, its namespaces and records. Load when asked about 'this venue'.

content.inline:
## Venue
A venue is one Covia grid node: a running server with its own DID that hosts operations, agents, assets and users' data, and federates with other venues. Public facts live under `v/` — never guess, read.

Call the venue configuration tool for the curated effective settings that change how you should work here: agent defaults, Job-recording policy, storage durability, protocols, limits, validation, active adapters and their explicitly public settings. It deliberately omits private paths, network allow-lists, modules, credentials and secret references.

Identity and address (`read {path}`):
- `v/info/name`, `v/info/did` (canonical identity; a `did:web` alias may be declared), `v/info/url` (base URL — the address to give a human), `v/info/version`, `v/info/started`, `v/info/protocols` (rest, mcp, a2a; `dlfs-webdav` when mounted).

How a human or client connects, relative to `v/info/url`: REST `<url>/api/v1/…` (OpenAPI at `<url>/swagger`), MCP `<url>/mcp`, A2A card `<url>/.well-known/agent-card.json`, DID document `<url>/.well-known/did.json`. WebDAV: `v/info/adapters/dlfs/webdav` gives `enabled`, the mount `url`, and `windows` — the UNC path for mapping a drive on Windows (append the drive name).

What it offers:
- `v/info/adapters` — every active adapter with description and operation paths. Each adapter also owns `v/adapters/<name>/`: `info` (its public facts), `config` (only settings the adapter explicitly allow-lists as public), and its `ops/`, `skills/`, `templates/` — the complete public view of one adapter in one place; the same values as the canonical catalog, equally invocable.
- `v/info/modules` — loaded modules (optional adapters such as sql, python, telegram).
- `v/ops/<adapter>/<op>` — the operation catalog (schemas are the calling contract); `v/skills`, `v/agents/templates`. The discovery skill goes deeper.

Namespaces (paths you will see): `v/` venue globals · `w/` your workspace · `o/` your pinned operations · `a/` content-addressed assets · `s/` your secrets (names only, values never readable) · `g/` your agents · `j/` durable top-level and explicitly recorded Jobs · `h/` your human-in-the-loop inbox · `n/`, `t/` scratch. Inline agent tool calls do not create child Jobs; their calls and results remain audited in the session and timeline. Another user's data needs a delegated capability.

Rules: the venue's DID identifies it; its URL locates it — a `did:key` alone has no address. Other venues: grid skill. Who you are here: auth skill.
